schemes.label: Catalogue
schemes.about: Formal designations, as surveys write them. Planets take Roman numerals by orbit (the default) and their moons letters. Stars are SX and a running number, or SX J and their sky position; the components of a multiple star are A, B, C; surface features take the IAU's Latin descriptor terms with the world's name and a number. Every designation follows its parent's name when that is renamed. Sources: IAU naming rules, Hessman et al. 2010 (arXiv:1012.0707), the Washington Multiplicity Catalog, and the USGS and IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (docs/citations/naming.md).

schemes.label: Catalogue (letters)
schemes.about: Formal designations, as surveys write them. Planets take letters from b (the IAU's form) and their moons Roman numerals (as Kepler-1625 b I). Stars are SX and a running number, or SX J and their sky position; the components of a multiple star are A, B, C; surface features take the IAU's Latin descriptor terms with the world's name and a number. Every designation follows its parent's name when that is renamed. Sources: IAU naming rules, Hessman et al. 2010 (arXiv:1012.0707), the Washington Multiplicity Catalog, and the USGS and IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (docs/citations/naming.md).

schemes.label: English-sounding
schemes.about: Names built the way English place names are: a first element and an ending, each a real Old English or Norse place-name element with what it meant (Ash + ton, 'ash tree farmstead'), sometimes with Great, Little, North or Upper before it. Craters may take the surnames of long-dead British astronomers and explorers. The meanings are our own short glosses, citing Blackie 1887. First pass, corrections welcome.

schemes.label: Oluen
schemes.about: A soft, flowing tongue of open syllables and long vowels, with no hard stops. The thing comes first and the describing word after it. An original invented language (base-names, NM3d); not from any published setting.

schemes.label: Vesh
schemes.about: A hive-building people's tongue. Guttural, with one click and doubled stops. Short hard words; the describing word comes first, the thing last. An original invented language (base-names, NM3d); not from any published setting.

say.gh: a voiced kh, like a gargle
say.q: a k made far back in the throat

about: SSE4's built-in name schemes (naming design 4.8): Catalogue designations in two forms, and the avoid list that generated names are checked against (best effort: no list catches every word in every language or every trade mark, so every name can be renamed by hand).
